pr.task: Write aspect(w, h) returning the simplified aspect ratio as a string like '16:9'. Note: 16:10 should stay '16:10' when the simplified form is 8:5.
pr.taskz: 写函数 aspect(w,h) 回传化简后的长宽比字串；若化简为 8:5 则写成 16:10。
pr.solution:
import math

def aspect(w, h):
    g = math.gcd(w, h)
    a, b = w // g, h // g
    if (a, b) == (8, 5):
        a, b = 16, 10
    return f'{a}:{b}'

cards.en:
Idea: The system unit is the 'box' of a desktop computer. Think of it as a house: the motherboard is the floor plan that joins every room, the CPU is the brain, the PSU is the electricity meter.

What is inside:

ComponentJob
Motherboardplatform that connects all components
Processor (CPU, GPU)processes data and instructions; CPU controls the computer
Main memory (RAM, ROM)RAM: data for processing now; ROM: firmware to start the computer
Secondary storagekeeps data for future use
Interface cardse.g. graphics card, network card
Power supply unit (PSU)gives power to every part

Keyboard, mouse, monitor and printer are outside the system unit (peripherals).

Exam wording: The motherboard serves as a platform to connect all the components. RAM stores data temporarily for processing; ROM stores firmware required to start a computer. Secondary storage stores data for future use. The PSU provides power to the computer.
cards.zh:
直觉：System unit 就是台式机的“主机箱”。像一间屋：motherboard 是把所有房间连起来的地基，CPU 是大脑，PSU 是供电。

组件作用
Motherboard连接所有组件的平台
Processor（CPU、GPU）处理数据和指令；CPU 控制整部电脑
Main memory（RAM、ROM）RAM：暂存正在处理的数据；ROM：存放开机用的 firmware
Secondary storage长期保存数据
Interface cards例如显卡、网卡
PSU为电脑供电

键盘、鼠标、显示器属于主机外面的 peripherals。

考试写法：Motherboard serves as a platform to connect all the components. RAM stores data temporarily for processing. ROM stores firmware required to start a computer.

ex.q: Name the component: (i) keeps your essay after power off; (ii) holds the game data you are playing now; (iii) turns mains power into power the parts can use.
ex.a:
1. Kept after power off, for future use → secondary storage (e.g. SSD).
  2. Data in use right now → RAM.
  3. Gives power → PSU.
ex.az:
1. 关机后仍保存、将来用 → secondary storage。
  2. 正在用的数据 → RAM。
  3. 供电 → PSU。

ex.q: Which of these are inside the system unit: monitor, RAM, keyboard, SSD, graphics card?
ex.a:
1. Check each item: is it in the box or plugged in from outside?
  2. Inside: RAM, SSD, graphics card.
  3. Outside (peripherals): monitor, keyboard.
ex.az:
1. 逐个判断是在机箱内还是外接。
  2. 机箱内：RAM、SSD、graphics card。
  3. 外部：monitor、keyboard。

ex.q: A student writes: 'ROM stores data temporarily for processing.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. This mixes up RAM and ROM.
  2. RAM stores data temporarily for processing.
  3. ROM stores firmware (instructions) required to start a computer.
ex.az:
1. 这是把 RAM 和 ROM 搞混了。
  2. RAM 才是暂存处理中的数据。
  3. ROM 存放开机所需的 firmware。

frames.en: The motherboard sits at the centre; every part plugs into it.
frames.zh: Motherboard 在中间，所有部件都插在它上面。

frames.en: The CPU processes; RAM holds what it is working on now.
frames.zh: CPU 负责处理；RAM 存放正在处理的数据。

frames.en: Secondary storage keeps files after power off.
frames.zh: Secondary storage 关机后仍保存文件。

frames.en: The PSU powers everything.
frames.zh: PSU 为所有部件供电。

cards.t: Which components must a system unit have?
cards.en:
Idea: Ask 'Can the computer still work without it?' If yes, it is optional.

Must haveNot a must
CPU, RAM, motherboard, PSU, at least one secondary storage devicehard disk (an SSD can replace it), dedicated graphics card (an iGPU can replace it), optical drive, RAID

RAM cannot be replaced: the CPU needs it to hold the data in use.

Exam wording: A dedicated graphics card is not a must, because an iGPU can be used instead. A hard disk is not a must, because an SSD can be used as secondary storage.
cards.zh:
直觉：问自己“没有它电脑还能运行吗？”能 → 不是必须。

必须不一定
CPU、RAM、motherboard、PSU、至少一个 secondary storagehard disk（可用 SSD 代替）、独立显卡（可用 iGPU）、光驱、RAID

RAM 无法被代替，CPU 必须用它暂存数据。

考试写法：A dedicated graphics card is not a must, because an iGPU can be used instead.

ex.q: Must a system unit have a hard disk?
ex.a:
1. It must have some secondary storage.
  2. But it can be an SSD.
  3. So: No, a hard disk is not a must.
ex.az:
1. 必须有某种 secondary storage。
  2. 但可以是 SSD。
  3. 所以 hard disk 不是必须。

ex.q: Must a system unit have RAM?
ex.a:
1. The CPU needs somewhere fast to hold the data and instructions in use.
  2. Nothing else can do this job.
  3. So: Yes, RAM is a must.
ex.az:
1. CPU 需要地方暂存正在用的数据和指令。
  2. 其他部件不能代替。
  3. 所以 RAM 必须有。

ex.q: 'Every computer must have a graphics card to show images.' True?
ex.a:
1. This is a common mistake.
  2. A display can be driven by an iGPU in the CPU or motherboard chipset.
  3. So a dedicated graphics card is not a must.
ex.az:
1. 常见错误。
  2. iGPU 也能输出画面。
  3. 所以独立显卡不是必须。

cards.en:
Idea: A motherboard is like a power strip with many different sockets. Each socket shape is made for one kind of device.

A motherboard is a circuit board that provides slots and ports for connecting components and peripheral devices.

Slot / portDevices
SATA slothard disks, SSD
PCIe slotgraphics card, sound card, network interface card (NIC)
USB portmouse, keyboard, USB flash drive
VGA / HDMI portmonitor, projector
M.2 portmost things SATA/PCIe/USB can connect, e.g. SSD

Modern motherboards often have integrated interfaces (network, graphics, sound) built in.

Exam wording: A motherboard is a circuit board that provides slots and ports for connecting electrical components and peripheral devices.
cards.zh:
直觉：主板像一个有很多不同插孔的拖板，每种插孔对应一类设备。

Motherboard 是提供 slots 和 ports 来连接组件和外部设备的电路板。

插槽/端口设备
SATAhard disk、SSD
PCIe显卡、声卡、NIC
USB鼠标、键盘、U 盘
VGA / HDMI显示器、投影机
M.2SSD 等多数设备

新主板常内置网络、图形、声音接口（integrated interfaces）。

考试写法：A motherboard provides slots and ports for connecting components and peripheral devices.

ex.q: Which slot/port for: (i) a new graphics card; (ii) a projector; (iii) a 2 TB hard disk?
ex.a:
1. Graphics card → PCIe slot.
  2. Projector → HDMI/VGA port.
  3. Hard disk → SATA slot.
ex.az:
1. 显卡 → PCIe。
  2. 投影机 → HDMI/VGA。
  3. 硬盘 → SATA。

ex.q: A computer has no network card but can go online with a cable. Why?
ex.a:
1. The motherboard may have an integrated network interface.
  2. So no separate NIC in a PCIe slot is needed.
ex.az:
1. 主板可能内置网络接口。
  2. 所以不需另装 NIC。

ex.q: 'Connect the monitor to the SATA slot.' What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. SATA is for secondary storage, not display units.
  2. A monitor uses the HDMI or VGA port.
ex.az:
1. SATA 是接储存设备的。
  2. 显示器要接 HDMI 或 VGA。

cards.en:
Idea: The CPU is the 'brain'. It reads instructions one by one and tells the other parts what to do.

  • A CPU processes data and instructions and controls most operations of the computer.
  • It makes a lot of heat, so it needs a cooling fan or heat sink (on the photo, the CPU is under the fan).
  • CPU and GPU usually use the most energy in the system unit, so check them when choosing a PSU.

Exam wording: The CPU processes data and instructions and controls most of the operations performed by a computer. A cooling fan / heat sink prevents the CPU from overheating.
cards.zh:
直觉：CPU 是电脑的“大脑”，逐条读指令并指挥其他部件。

  • CPU 处理数据和指令，控制电脑大部分运作。
  • 会产生大量热，需要 cooling fan / heat sink。
  • CPU 和 GPU 通常最耗电，选 PSU 时要考虑。

考试写法：The CPU processes data and instructions and controls most of the operations performed by a computer.

ex.q: Why is there a fan on top of the CPU?
ex.a:
1. The CPU makes much heat when processing.
  2. Too hot → it may slow down or be damaged.
  3. The fan/heat sink prevents overheating.
ex.az:
1. CPU 工作时产生大量热。
  2. 过热会降速或损坏。
  3. 风扇/散热片防止过热。

ex.q: Which two components should you check first when estimating power needed for a PSU?
ex.a:
1. Find the biggest energy users.
  2. They are the CPU and GPU.
ex.az:
1. 找最耗电的部件。
  2. CPU 和 GPU。

ex.q: 'The CPU stores all the files of the computer.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The CPU processes, it does not keep files.
  2. Files are kept in secondary storage; data in use is in RAM.
ex.az:
1. CPU 只负责处理，不储存文件。
  2. 文件存在 secondary storage。

cards.tz: GPU 与 CPU 的分别
cards.en:
Idea: A CPU is like a few smart professors who can do any job. A GPU is like hundreds of students who each do one simple sum at the same time. For drawing millions of pixels, the many students win.

CPUGPU
Made formany types of tasksgraphic rendering
Coresfewermore cores, good at doing many simple jobs at once
  • A GPU frees up the computing power of the CPU for other tasks.
  • GPUs are used to train artificial intelligence / deep learning, which needs lots of data processed at the same time.
  • A GPU also needs cooling.

Exam wording: A GPU is more specialised in graphic rendering, while a CPU handles various types of tasks. A GPU has more cores, so it is more capable of multitasking.
cards.zh:
直觉：CPU 像几位什么都会的教授；GPU 像几百个学生同时各算一道简单算术。画几百万个像素时，学生多的一方胜。

CPUGPU
用途各种工作graphic rendering
核心较少较多，适合同时做大量简单运算
  • GPU 可释放 CPU 的运算能力。
  • GPU 是训练 deep learning 的核心。

考试写法：A GPU has more cores and is thus more capable of multitasking.

ex.q: Why does a video-editing PC benefit from a strong GPU?
ex.a:
1. Video editing renders many frames of pixels.
  2. A GPU has many cores to do these simple calculations at the same time.
  3. The CPU is freed up for other tasks, so the work is faster.
ex.az:
1. 剪片要渲染大量像素。
  2. GPU 核心多可同时计算。
  3. CPU 也被释放，整体更快。

ex.q: Why are GPUs used to train deep learning models?
ex.a:
1. Training needs a huge amount of data processed quickly.
  2. Most steps are simple sums that can run in parallel.
  3. A GPU's many cores do this well.
ex.az:
1. 训练需快速处理海量数据。
  2. 多数是可并行的简单运算。
  3. GPU 核心多正好适合。

ex.q: 'A GPU can fully replace the CPU because it has more cores.' True?
ex.a:
1. No. More cores does not mean it can do every type of task.
  2. The GPU is specialised for graphics/parallel work; the CPU still controls the computer and runs general tasks.
ex.az:
1. 错。
  2. GPU 是专门化的，CPU 仍负责控制和一般工作。

cards.en:
Idea: A graphics card is a separate 'mini computer for pictures' with its own memory. An iGPU is a small GPU built into the CPU or motherboard chipset, sharing what is already there.

A graphics card has a GPU plus:

  • its own RAM used only for graphics;
  • a digital-to-analog converter (DAC) that turns results into analog signals for monitors/projectors.
Graphics cardiGPU
Strengthhigher graphics processing powerlower cost, lower energy consumption
Weaknesscostly, uses more energylower graphics processing power
Good forCAD, video editing, gamingword processing, web

Exam wording: An iGPU is a GPU integrated into the chipset of a motherboard or a CPU. A graphics card provides higher graphics processing power.
cards.zh:
直觉：显卡是一块独立的“图像小电脑”，有自己的记忆体；iGPU 是内置在 CPU 或主板芯片组里的小 GPU。

Graphics card = GPU + 专用 RAM + DAC（把结果转成模拟信号给显示器）。

独立显卡iGPU
优点图形处理能力高便宜、省电
缺点贵、耗电图形处理能力低
适合CAD、剪片、游戏文书处理

考试写法：An iGPU is a GPU integrated into the chipset of a motherboard or a CPU.

ex.q: A secretary does word processing; a student does 3D animation. Recommend for each.
ex.a:
1. Secretary: little graphics needed → iGPU, lower cost and energy.
  2. Student: heavy rendering → graphics card, higher graphics processing power.
ex.az:
1. 秘书 → iGPU，便宜省电。
  2. 3D 动画 → 独立显卡，图形能力高。

ex.q: Name two parts on a graphics card besides the GPU and give their use.
ex.a:
1. RAM: memory only for graphics processing.
  2. DAC: converts results into analog signals for display units.
ex.az:
1. RAM：图形专用记忆体。
  2. DAC：转成模拟信号给显示设备。

ex.q: 'An iGPU is a small graphics card plugged into a PCIe slot.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: that is a dedicated card.
  2. An iGPU is integrated into the CPU or motherboard chipset, no slot needed.
ex.az:
1. 错：插 PCIe 的是独立显卡。
  2. iGPU 是集成在 CPU 或芯片组里的。

cards.t: Storage device overview: main memory vs secondary storage
cards.tz: 储存设备概览：主存储器 vs 辅助存储器
cards.en:
Idea: Main memory is your desk (things you use right now). Secondary storage is your bookshelf (things you keep).

Volatile = data is lost when power is off. Non-volatile = data stays.

RAMROMSecondary storage
Groupmain memorymain memorysecondary
Volatile?volatilenon-volatilenon-volatile
Rewritefastusually notyes
Usedata for processing nowfirmware to startdata for future use

Exam wording: Main memory (primary storage) refers to RAM and ROM. RAM is volatile: data disappears once the computer shuts down. Secondary storage is non-volatile.
cards.zh:
直觉：Main memory 像书桌（正在用的东西），secondary storage 像书架（保存的东西）。

Volatile：断电数据消失；non-volatile：断电仍保存。

RAMROMSecondary
Volatile?是否否
可改写快速可写通常不可可
用途暂存处理中数据开机 firmware将来用的数据

考试写法：RAM is volatile; ROM and secondary storage are non-volatile.

ex.q: Power cuts while you type an unsaved document. What is lost and why?
ex.a:
1. Unsaved work is only in RAM.
  2. RAM is volatile, so it is lost.
  3. The last saved copy on secondary storage stays.
ex.az:
1. 未保存内容只在 RAM。
  2. RAM 是 volatile，所以丢失。
  3. 已保存版本仍在 secondary storage。

ex.q: Classify: SSD, RAM, ROM, USB flash drive → main memory or secondary storage?
ex.a:
1. Main memory: RAM, ROM.
  2. Secondary: SSD, USB flash drive.
ex.az:
1. Main：RAM、ROM。
  2. Secondary：SSD、U 盘。

ex.q: 'ROM is volatile because it is main memory.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Being main memory does not make it volatile.
  2. Only RAM is volatile; ROM is non-volatile, so the firmware stays after shutdown.
ex.az:
1. 是 main memory 不等于 volatile。
  2. ROM 是 non-volatile。

cards.en:
Idea: The wall socket gives strong alternating current. Computer chips need weak, steady direct current. The PSU is the 'translator'.

  • PSU converts high-voltage alternating current (AC) to low-voltage direct current (DC).
  • Power is measured in watts (W).
  • It needs a cooling fan / heat sink.
  • Before building a PC, add up the energy use of the parts (CPU and GPU use the most) and choose a PSU with enough watts plus some spare.

Exam wording: A PSU converts high-voltage AC to low-voltage DC, which provides suitable power for the computer to operate.
cards.zh:
直觉：墙上插座是高压交流电，芯片需要低压直流电，PSU 负责“转换”。

  • PSU 把 high-voltage AC 转成 low-voltage DC。
  • 功率单位 W。
  • 需要散热。
  • 组装前要估算各部件耗电（CPU、GPU 最多），选功率足够并有余量的 PSU。

考试写法：A PSU converts high-voltage AC to low-voltage DC.

ex.q: CPU 125 W, GPU 220 W, others 100 W. Choose a PSU: 400 W, 550 W or 1200 W?
ex.a:
1. Total = 125 + 220 + 100 = 445 W.
  2. 400 W is too small.
  3. 550 W covers it with spare (~24%); 1200 W is far more than needed and costs more.
  4. Choose 550 W.
ex.az:
1. 总和 = 445 W。
  2. 400 W 不够。
  3. 550 W 足够并有余量；1200 W 过多。
  4. 选 550 W。

ex.q: Why can't chips use mains power directly?
ex.a:
1. Mains is high-voltage AC.
  2. Chips need low-voltage DC.
  3. The PSU converts it.
ex.az:
1. 市电是高压交流。
  2. 芯片要低压直流。
  3. PSU 负责转换。

ex.q: 'The PSU converts DC to AC for the computer.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Direction is reversed.
  2. It converts AC (high voltage) to DC (low voltage).
ex.az:
1. 方向反了。
  2. 应是 AC → DC。

cards.en:
Idea: A bus is a road inside the computer. Data and signals are the cars. Wider roads carry more cars at once.

  • Buses connect components by transferring data and control signals.
  • Some connect internal parts (CPU ↔ main memory); others connect the system unit to external devices.
  • A system bus transfers data and control signals between processors and components.
  • Bus width = how much data a bus moves at a time; usually equal to the CPU's word length.
  • The system bus has three parts: control bus, address bus, data bus.

Exam wording: The system bus transfers data and control signals between processors and various components. Bus width is usually the same as the word length of the CPU.
cards.zh:
直觉：Bus 是电脑里的公路，数据和信号是车；路越宽一次过的车越多。

  • Bus 传送数据和控制信号来连接各组件。
  • System bus 在处理器和各组件之间传送数据和控制信号。
  • Bus width：一次能传多少数据，通常等于 CPU 的 word length。
  • System bus 分三部分：control bus、address bus、data bus。

考试写法：Bus width is usually the same as the word length of the CPU.

ex.q: A CPU has a 64-bit word length. What is the likely data bus width, and how many bytes move at a time?
ex.a:
1. Bus width ≈ word length = 64 bits.
  2. 64 ÷ 8 = 8 bytes per transfer.
ex.az:
1. Bus width ≈ 64 bits。
  2. 64÷8 = 8 bytes。

ex.q: Name the three parts of the system bus.
ex.a:
1. Control bus
  2. Address bus
  3. Data bus
ex.az:
1. Control bus
  2. Address bus
  3. Data bus

ex.q: 'USB is one of the three parts of the system bus.' True?
ex.a:
1. No. USB connects external devices.
  2. The three parts are control, address and data bus.
ex.az:
1. 错，USB 用来接外部设备。
  2. 三部分是 control、address、data bus。

frames.en: CPU, main memory and I/O devices share the system bus.
frames.zh: CPU、主存和 I/O 设备共用 system bus。

frames.en: Data travels between CPU and memory along the bus.
frames.zh: 数据经 bus 在 CPU 和内存间传送。

frames.en: The same bus reaches I/O devices.
frames.zh: 同一 bus 也连到 I/O 设备。

cards.t: Control bus, address bus and data bus
cards.en:
Idea: Ordering food: the address says which table, the control signal says 'serve now' or 'take back', and the data is the food going either way.

BusCarriesDirection
Control buscontrol signals (read/write, timing)one-way: processor → components
Address busmemory addressesone-way: processor → components
Data busdata or instructionstwo-way
  • Control bus ensures the correct timing of data transfer.
  • Address bus indicates which data to fetch or store.
  • Trap: right object but wrong direction is wrong.

Exam wording: The address bus carries memory addresses one-way from the processor. The data bus is two-way. The control bus carries control signals to ensure the correct timing of data transfer.
cards.zh:
直觉：点餐：address 是几号桌，control 是“上菜/收回”的指令，data 是双向来回的菜。

Bus传送方向
Control控制信号单向：处理器→组件
Address内存地址单向：处理器→组件
Data数据或指令双向

陷阱：内容对但方向错，也是错。

考试写法：The address bus is one-way; the data bus is two-way.

ex.q: CPU reads a value from RAM address 2040. Which bus carries what?
ex.a:
1. Control bus: the read signal (CPU → RAM).
  2. Address bus: 2040 (CPU → RAM).
  3. Data bus: the value (RAM → CPU).
ex.az:
1. Control：read 信号。
  2. Address：2040。
  3. Data：数值由 RAM 回到 CPU。

ex.q: Which bus is two-way and why?
ex.a:
1. The data bus.
  2. The CPU both reads data from and writes data to memory.
ex.az:
1. Data bus。
  2. CPU 要读也要写。

ex.q: 'The address bus transfers addresses from memory to the CPU.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Object correct, direction wrong.
  2. Addresses go from the processor to memory (one-way).
ex.az:
1. 内容对，方向错。
  2. 地址只由处理器送往内存。

demo.title: One memory read on the three buses

frames.en: CPU puts the address on the address bus (one-way).
frames.zh: CPU 把地址放上 address bus（单向）。

frames.en: CPU sends a 'read' signal on the control bus.
frames.zh: CPU 经 control bus 发出 read 信号。

frames.en: RAM returns the data on the data bus (two-way).
frames.zh: RAM 经 data bus 把数据传回（双向）。

cards.tz: SATA 与 PCIe 总线（增润）
cards.en:
Idea: Different devices use different 'lanes'. Storage uses the SATA lane; fast expansion cards use the PCIe lane.

  • SATA bus (serial advanced technology attachment): connects secondary storage like hard disks, SSDs and optical disc drives.
  • PCIe bus (peripheral component interconnect express): connects graphics cards, sound cards, NICs; allows high-speed data transfer.
  • Neither is part of the control/address/data trio.

Exam wording: SATA connects secondary storage devices; PCIe connects graphics cards, sound cards and NICs at high speed.
cards.zh:
直觉：不同设备走不同“车道”：储存走 SATA，高速扩展卡走 PCIe。

  • SATA：接 hard disk、SSD、光驱。
  • PCIe：接显卡、声卡、NIC，传输速度高。
  • 两者都不是 control/address/data 三者之一。

考试写法：SATA connects secondary storage; PCIe connects graphics cards, sound cards and NICs.

ex.q: A SATA SSD transfers at about 550 MB/s. How long to copy a 2.2 GB (= 2200 MB) video?
ex.a:
1. Time = size ÷ rate.
  2. 2200 ÷ 550 = 4 s (ideal, ignoring overhead).

ex.q: Match: optical drive, sound card → SATA or PCIe?
ex.a:
1. Optical drive is storage → SATA.
  2. Sound card is an expansion card → PCIe.
ex.az:
1. 光驱 → SATA。
  2. 声卡 → PCIe。

ex.q: 'PCIe carries control signals as part of the system bus.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: PCIe is an expansion bus.
  2. Control signals in the system bus go on the control bus.
ex.az:
1. 错。
  2. 控制信号走 control bus。

cards.en:
Idea: USB is the 'universal plug' for outside devices. You can plug in and pull out while the computer is on.

  • Connects keyboards, mice, printers, webcams, scanners, external storage.
  • Hot swapping: plug in or swap devices while the computer is still operating.
  • Connectors: USB-A (most PC ports), micro-USB (older phones), USB-C (reversible).
  • Version by colour: USB 1.0 white, 2.0 black, 3.0 blue. USB 3.0 has a higher data transfer rate.

Exam wording: USB supports hot swapping: users can plug in or swap devices while the computer system is still operating.
cards.zh:
直觉：USB 是外部设备的“万用插头”，开机时可直接插拔。

  • 接键盘、鼠标、打印机、摄像头、外置储存。
  • Hot swapping：电脑运行中也能插拔设备。
  • 接口：USB-A、micro-USB、USB-C（正反可插）。
  • 颜色：1.0 白、2.0 黑、3.0 蓝；3.0 传输率更高。

考试写法：USB supports hot swapping.

ex.q: Port A is black, port B is blue. Which is faster for copying to a flash drive?
ex.a:
1. Black = USB 2.0, blue = USB 3.0.
  2. USB 3.0 has a higher data transfer rate.
  3. Use port B.

ex.q: Give two uses of a USB port.
ex.a:
1. Connect a keyboard/mouse.
  2. Store data on a USB flash drive (or install an OS from it).
ex.az:
1. 接键盘/鼠标。
  2. 存数据到 U 盘。

ex.q: 'Hot swapping means USB devices are hot, so let them cool down.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Not about temperature.
  2. It means you can connect or remove a device while the computer is running.
ex.az:
1. 与温度无关。
  2. 指运行中可插拔。

cards.t: CPU components: CU, ALU and registers
cards.en:
Idea: In a kitchen, the CU is the head chef who reads the recipe and gives orders; the ALU is the cook who chops and mixes; registers are the tiny plates right next to the stove.

  • Control Unit (CU): decodes instructions, controls how the ALU and other devices respond, and controls the data flow between CPU and other parts.
  • Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU): executes instructions. Arithmetic: + − × ÷. Logical: compare (=, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥), AND, OR, NOT. The result goes to the accumulator.
  • Registers: very small, very fast memory inside the CPU.

Exam wording: The CU decodes instructions and controls the data flow; the ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
cards.zh:
直觉：厨房里 CU 是读食谱、下命令的主厨；ALU 是动手切菜炒菜的厨师；registers 是炉边的小碟子。

  • CU：解码指令，控制 ALU 及其他设备的反应和数据流。
  • ALU：执行指令，做算术（+ − × ÷）和逻辑运算（比较、AND、OR、NOT），结果送到 accumulator。
  • Registers：CPU 内极小极快的记忆体。

考试写法：The CU decodes instructions; the ALU executes them (arithmetic and logical operations).

ex.q: Which unit handles: (i) 25 > 18? (ii) 7 × 6? (iii) deciding which data goes to the printer?
ex.a:
1. Comparison → ALU (logical).
  2. Multiplication → ALU (arithmetic).
  3. Controlling data flow → CU.
ex.az:
1. 比较 → ALU。
  2. 乘法 → ALU。
  3. 控制数据流 → CU。

ex.q: Is NOT (A AND B) handled by the CU or ALU?
ex.a:
1. AND and NOT are logical operations.
  2. So the ALU.
ex.az:
1. 属于逻辑运算。
  2. ALU。

ex.q: 'The ALU decodes the instruction and the CU executes it.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Roles swapped.
  2. CU decodes, ALU executes.
ex.az:
1. 角色对调了。
  2. CU 解码，ALU 执行。

cards.t: Registers: CIR, PC, MAR, MDR, accumulator
cards.en:
Idea: Registers are sticky notes the CPU keeps on its desk. Each note has one job.

RegisterHolds
PC (program counter)the address of the next instruction
MAR (memory address register)the memory address to read or write; linked to memory by the address bus
MDR (memory data register)the data/instruction read from or written to memory; linked by the data bus
CIR (current instruction register)the instruction being executed now
Accumulator (ACC)the result from the ALU

Registers are few and small (usually 32 or 64 bits), but the fastest memory.

Exam wording: The PC stores the address of the next instruction to be executed. The MAR stores the memory address to be read from or written into. The MDR stores the data read from or written into memory.
cards.zh:
直觉：Registers 是 CPU 桌上的便利贴，每张只做一件事。

寄存器存放
PC下一条指令的地址
MAR要读/写的内存地址（经 address bus）
MDR读出/写入的数据或指令（经 data bus）
CIR正在执行的指令
AccumulatorALU 的结果

数量少、容量小（通常 32 或 64 bits），但最快。

考试写法：The PC stores the address of the next instruction to be executed.

ex.q: PC = 205. The CPU starts fetching. What goes into the MAR, and what is the PC after it is updated?
ex.a:
1. PC's address is copied: MAR = 205.
  2. PC is updated to the next instruction: PC = 206 (one instruction per address).
ex.az:
1. MAR = 205。
  2. PC 更新为 206。

ex.q: Which register is connected to memory by (i) the address bus, (ii) the data bus?
ex.a:
1. Address bus → MAR.
  2. Data bus → MDR.
ex.az:
1. Address bus → MAR。
  2. Data bus → MDR。

ex.q: 'The PC counts how many programs are running.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The name misleads.
  2. The PC holds the address of the next instruction.
ex.az:
1. 名字误导。
  2. PC 存下一条指令的地址。

frames.en: The address in the PC (e.g. 100) is copied to the MAR.
frames.zh: PC 中的地址（如 100）复制到 MAR。

frames.en: PC becomes 101, the address of the next instruction.
frames.zh: PC 更新为 101，即下一条指令的地址。

frames.en: MAR sends address 100 to RAM on the address bus.
frames.zh: MAR 经 address bus 把地址 100 送到 RAM。

frames.en: RAM sends the instruction at 100 to the MDR on the data bus.
frames.zh: RAM 经 data bus 把地址 100 的指令送到 MDR。

frames.en: The instruction is copied into the CIR.
frames.zh: 指令复制到 CIR。

frames.en: The CU decodes it; the ALU executes it.
frames.zh: CU 解码；ALU 执行。

frames.en: The result goes into the accumulator.
frames.zh: 结果存入 accumulator。

cards.en:
Idea: You keep the books you use every day on your desk, not in the library. Cache is the CPU's desk shelf for data it will probably need again.

  • Cache memory is inside the CPU, volatile, and faster than RAM.
  • It temporarily stores the data or instructions expected to be accessed most frequently.
  • Path: CPU ↔ cache ↔ RAM ↔ secondary storage. The CPU never reads secondary storage directly.
  • Speed: register > cache > RAM > SSD > hard disk > tape.

Exam wording: Cache memory temporarily stores data or instructions that are expected to be accessed most frequently, so the CPU accesses them faster than from RAM.
cards.zh:
直觉：每天要用的书放在书桌上，不放在图书馆。Cache 就是 CPU 的“桌边书架”。

  • Cache 在 CPU 内，volatile，比 RAM 快。
  • 暂存预计最常被存取的数据或指令。
  • 路径：CPU ↔ cache ↔ RAM ↔ secondary storage；CPU 不直接读 secondary storage。

考试写法：Cache memory temporarily stores data or instructions that are expected to be accessed most frequently.

ex.q: Cache access takes 1 ns, RAM 60 ns. The CPU reads the same value 10 times; it is in cache after the first RAM read. Total time?
ex.a:
1. 1st read from RAM: 60 ns (copy into cache).
  2. 9 more reads from cache: 9 × 1 = 9 ns.
  3. Total = 69 ns, vs 10 × 60 = 600 ns without cache.
ex.az:
1. 第 1 次 RAM：60 ns。
  2. 其后 9 次 cache：9 ns。
  3. 共 69 ns；没 cache 要 600 ns。

ex.q: Is cache volatile? What happens on shutdown?
ex.a:
1. Yes, cache is volatile like RAM.
  2. Its contents are lost.
ex.az:
1. 是 volatile。
  2. 关机后内容消失。

ex.q: 'The CPU loads programs straight from the SSD into cache.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Data must first be loaded into main memory (RAM).
  2. Then cache copies frequently used parts.
ex.az:
1. 必须先载入 RAM。
  2. 再由 cache 暂存常用部分。

demo.title: Where does the CPU find data?

frames.en: The CPU first looks in cache (fast).
frames.zh: CPU 先查 cache（快）。

frames.en: If not in cache, read RAM and keep a copy in cache.
frames.zh: cache 没有就读 RAM，并复制一份到 cache。

frames.en: If the program is not in RAM, it is loaded from secondary storage into RAM first.
frames.zh: 程序未载入时，先由 secondary storage 载入 RAM。

cards.en:
Idea: Like following a recipe: read the next line, understand it, do it, write down the result, repeat.

Most computers use the von Neumann architecture. The machine cycle (instruction cycle) has 4 phases:

  1. Fetch: the instruction is fetched from main memory (RAM) to the CPU.
  2. Decode: the CU decodes it.
  3. Execute: the ALU executes it.
  4. Store: the result is stored (accumulator / memory).

Then the cycle repeats for the next instruction.

Exam wording: The instruction is fetched from main memory, decoded by the CU, executed by the ALU, and the result is stored.
cards.zh:
直觉：像照食谱做菜：读下一行 → 看懂 → 照做 → 记下结果 → 重复。

大部分电脑用 von Neumann architecture，machine cycle 有四阶段：

  1. Fetch：从 main memory 取指令到 CPU。
  2. Decode：CU 解码。
  3. Execute：ALU 执行。
  4. Store：储存结果。

考试写法：Fetched from main memory, decoded by the CU, executed by the ALU, result stored.

ex.q: Instruction 'ADD 5' (add 5 to ACC = 10). Describe the four phases.
ex.a:
1. Fetch: 'ADD 5' is fetched from RAM.
  2. Decode: CU works out it means 'add 5 to the accumulator'.
  3. Execute: ALU computes 10 + 5 = 15.
  4. Store: ACC = 15.
ex.az:
1. Fetch：从 RAM 取 ADD 5。
  2. Decode：CU 解释为把 5 加到 ACC。
  3. Execute：ALU 算 10+5=15。
  4. Store：ACC=15。

ex.q: Which component does each phase: decode, execute?
ex.a:
1. Decode → CU.
  2. Execute → ALU.
ex.az:
1. Decode → CU。
  2. Execute → ALU。

ex.q: 'Instructions are fetched from the MAR.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The MAR only holds the address.
  2. Instructions are fetched from main memory.
ex.az:
1. MAR 只存地址。
  2. 指令从 main memory 取出。

frames.en: Get the instruction from RAM.
frames.zh: 从 RAM 取指令。

frames.en: CU works out what it means.
frames.zh: CU 解码。

frames.en: ALU does it.
frames.zh: ALU 执行。

frames.en: Save the result, then loop.
frames.zh: 储存结果，再循环。

cards.t: The seven steps of the machine cycle
cards.en:
Idea: Zoom into 'fetch': it is really a relay race of registers and buses.

StepWhat happens
1Address in PC is copied to MAR.
2PC is updated to the address of the next instruction.
3Address in MAR goes to main memory via the address bus.
4Instruction at that address goes from memory to MDR via the data bus.
5MDR is copied to CIR.
6CU decodes; ALU executes.
7Result stored in the accumulator.

Memory chain: PC → MAR → address bus → RAM → data bus → MDR → CIR → CU → ALU → ACC.

Exam wording: The memory address in the PC is copied to the MAR; the PC is incremented; the address is sent to main memory via the address bus; the instruction is transferred to the MDR via the data bus; then copied to the CIR.
cards.zh:
直觉：把 fetch 放大看，其实是寄存器和总线之间的接力赛。

  1. PC 的地址复制到 MAR。
  2. PC 更新为下一条指令地址。
  3. MAR 的地址经 address bus 送往内存。
  4. 内存把指令经 data bus 送到 MDR。
  5. MDR 复制到 CIR。
  6. CU 解码，ALU 执行。
  7. 结果存入 accumulator。

口诀：PC → MAR → address bus → RAM → data bus → MDR → CIR → CU → ALU → ACC。

考试写法：The address in the PC is copied to the MAR … transferred to the MDR via the data bus … copied to the CIR.

ex.q: Put in order: (A) MDR→CIR (B) PC→MAR (C) memory→MDR via data bus (D) MAR→memory via address bus (E) PC updated.
ex.a:
1. Start with PC → MAR: B.
  2. PC updated: E.
  3. Address sent: D.
  4. Instruction back: C.
  5. Copy to CIR: A.
  6. Answer: B, E, D, C, A.
ex.az:
1. B
  2. E
  3. D
  4. C
  5. A
  6. 答案 B E D C A。

ex.q: At step 5, PC = 301. What address was the current instruction fetched from (one instruction per address)?
ex.a:
1. PC was incremented at step 2.
  2. So the current instruction came from 300.
ex.az:
1. PC 在第 2 步已加 1。
  2. 当前指令来自 300。

ex.q: 'The instruction goes from memory to the CIR via the address bus.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Two errors.
  2. It goes to the MDR first, via the data bus, then is copied to the CIR.
ex.az:
1. 两处错。
  2. 先经 data bus 到 MDR，再复制到 CIR。

frames.en: The address in the PC (e.g. 100) is copied to the MAR.
frames.zh: PC 中的地址（如 100）复制到 MAR。

frames.en: PC becomes 101, the address of the next instruction.
frames.zh: PC 更新为 101，即下一条指令的地址。

frames.en: MAR sends address 100 to RAM on the address bus.
frames.zh: MAR 经 address bus 把地址 100 送到 RAM。

frames.en: RAM sends the instruction at 100 to the MDR on the data bus.
frames.zh: RAM 经 data bus 把地址 100 的指令送到 MDR。

frames.en: The instruction is copied into the CIR.
frames.zh: 指令复制到 CIR。

frames.en: The CU decodes it; the ALU executes it.
frames.zh: CU 解码；ALU 执行。

frames.en: The result goes into the accumulator.
frames.zh: 结果存入 accumulator。

cards.t: Visualising register contents in the machine cycle
cards.tz: 机器周期中寄存器内容的变化
cards.en:
Idea: Take a snapshot of every register after each step. It shows the PC is always one step ahead.

Example: instruction 'LOAD 7' is at address 100.

StagePCMARMDRCIR
0100
1100100
2101100
3101100
4101100LOAD 7
5–7101100LOAD 7LOAD 7

From stage 2, the PC already points to the next instruction while the current one is still being processed.

Exam wording: The PC is updated to the address of the next instruction before the current instruction is decoded and executed.
cards.zh:
直觉：每一步都给寄存器拍张“快照”，就会看到 PC 总是早一步。

例：地址 100 存放指令 LOAD 7。上表：阶段 1 MAR=100；阶段 2 PC=101；阶段 4 MDR=LOAD 7；阶段 5 CIR=LOAD 7。

从阶段 2 开始，PC 已指向下一条指令。

考试写法：The PC is updated before the current instruction is executed.

ex.q: At stage 4 in the table, what are PC, MAR and MDR?
ex.a:
1. PC = 101 (already updated).
  2. MAR = 100.
  3. MDR = LOAD 7 (just arrived via data bus).
ex.az:
1. PC=101。
  2. MAR=100。
  3. MDR=LOAD 7。

ex.q: When does the CIR first hold 'LOAD 7'?
ex.a:
1. Only after it is copied from MDR.
  2. That is stage 5.
ex.az:
1. 由 MDR 复制后。
  2. 阶段 5。

ex.q: 'At stage 6 the PC is 100 because instruction 100 is being executed.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Mixes up 'current' and 'next'.
  2. The CIR holds the current instruction; the PC = 101.
ex.az:
1. 混淆“当前”和“下一条”。
  2. PC 应为 101。

demo.src:
1 MAR <- PC
2 PC <- PC + 1
3 send MAR on address bus
4 MDR <- memory[MAR]
5 CIR <- MDR
6 decode and execute CIR
7 ACC <- result

cards.en:
Idea: The clock is a drummer. Each beat (clock cycle) the CPU can do a step. Faster drumming = more steps per second.

  • Clock rate = the number of clock cycles a CPU performs in one second (unit Hz).
  • Clock cycle time = 1 ÷ clock rate.
  • Higher clock rate → usually better performance but higher energy consumption; not linearly proportional.
RateValueTimeValue
kHz103ms10−3 s
MHz106µs10−6 s
GHz109ns10−9 s
ps10−12 s

Exam wording: Clock rate is the number of clock cycles a CPU performs in one second. A higher clock rate usually gives better performance, but the relationship is not linearly proportional.
cards.zh:
直觉：时钟像鼓手，每一拍 CPU 做一步；打得越快，每秒做的步越多。

  • Clock rate = CPU 每秒执行的 clock cycle 数（Hz）。
  • Clock cycle 时间 = 1 ÷ clock rate。
  • 频率高 → 通常较快但更耗电；并非线性正比。

单位：kHz=10³，MHz=10⁶，GHz=10⁹；ms=10⁻³ s，µs=10⁻⁶ s，ns=10⁻⁹ s，ps=10⁻¹² s。

考试写法：Clock rate is the number of clock cycles a CPU performs in one second.

ex.q: A CPU runs at 4 GHz. Find the clock cycle time.
ex.a:
1. 4 GHz = 4 × 109 cycles/s.
  2. Time = 1 ÷ (4 × 109) = 0.25 × 10−9 s.
  3. = 0.25 ns (= 250 ps).

ex.q: A clock cycle takes 0.5 ns. What is the clock rate?
'Upgrading from 2 GHz to 4 GHz makes every program twice as fast.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Clock rate is only one factor.
  2. RAM, storage speed and the task also limit speed.
  3. The relationship is not linearly proportional; it also uses more energy.
ex.az:
1. 频率只是因素之一。
  2. RAM、储存速度等也有限制。
  3. 非线性正比，且更耗电。

cards.en:
Idea: More cashiers in a shop serve more customers at the same time, but one customer is not served faster.

  • A core is an individual processor unit inside a CPU.
  • The number of cores determines the number of processes that can run at the same time.
  • More cores → better for multitasking, but not linearly proportional to speed: some work must be done in order.

Exam wording: A CPU with more cores usually performs better in multitasking, but the relationship with processing speed is not linearly proportional.
cards.zh:
直觉：店里收银员越多，同时能服务的顾客越多，但单个顾客不会更快。

  • Core：CPU 内独立的处理单元。
  • 核心数决定同时能运行的 process 数目。
  • 核心多 → 多工较佳，但与速度非线性正比：有些工作必须按次序。

考试写法：More cores usually perform better in multitasking; not linearly proportional.

ex.q: A job has 4 independent parts of 2 s each. Time on 1 core vs 4 cores?
ex.a:
1. 1 core: 4 × 2 = 8 s.
  2. 4 cores: all parts at once = 2 s (ideal).
ex.az:
1. 单核 8 秒。
  2. 四核 2 秒（理想）。

ex.q: Same 4 parts, but each needs the result of the one before. Time on 4 cores?
ex.a:
1. Parts must run one after another.
  2. Still 4 × 2 = 8 s; extra cores do not help.
ex.az:
1. 必须顺序执行。
  2. 仍是 8 秒。

ex.q: 'An 8-core CPU is always twice as fast as a 4-core CPU.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Only parallel work benefits.
  2. Sequential tasks and other parts limit speed; not linearly proportional.
ex.az:
1. 只有并行工作受惠。
  2. 非线性正比。

cards.en:
Idea: Word length is how big a 'bite' the CPU takes each time. A bigger bite also means it can count to bigger addresses.

  • Word length = the number of bits processed by a CPU each time. Usually 32 or 64 bits.
  • Registers and bus width usually match the word length.
  • An n-bit address can name 2n memory locations. Longer word → more memory can be addressed.
  • Performance is better, but not linearly proportional.

Exam wording: Word length is the number of bits processed by a CPU each time. A longer word length allows more memory locations to be addressed.
cards.zh:
直觉：Word length 是 CPU 每次“咬一口”的大小，口越大，能数到的地址也越大。

  • Word length：CPU 每次处理的 bit 数，通常 32 或 64。
  • Register 和 bus width 通常与之相同。
  • n 位地址可表示 2ⁿ 个位置；字长越长可寻址的内存越多。
  • 性能较好但非线性正比。

考试写法：Word length is the number of bits processed by a CPU each time.

ex.q: How many addresses can a 32-bit address name? If each holds 1 byte, how much memory?
ex.a:
1. 232 = 4 294 967 296 addresses.
  2. = 232 bytes = 4 GB (230 B = 1 GB, so 22 = 4).

ex.q: Unsigned range of one 16-bit word?
ex.a:
1. 216 = 65 536 values.
  2. Range 0 to 65 535.

ex.q: Word length is cut from 64 to 32 bits. 'It will definitely run slower and use less energy.' What must be true instead?
ex.a:
1. Speed and energy changes are not guaranteed.
  2. What must happen: it can address fewer memory locations (232 instead of 264).
ex.az:
1. 速度、耗电变化不一定。
  2. 一定的是：可寻址的内存位置减少。

cards.t: Misconception: 64-bit is not twice as efficient as 32-bit
cards.tz: 误解：64 位不是 32 位的两倍效率
cards.en:
Idea: A bigger truck does not make the trip twice as fast if the road is jammed.

  • Wrong: 'A 64-bit processor is twice as efficient as a 32-bit one.'
  • Right: a 64-bit processor can address more memory and handle more complex functions.
  • Clock rate, cores and word length are all not linearly proportional to performance, because RAM, storage and the task also limit speed.

Exam wording: The advantage of a 64-bit processor is that it can address more memory; the relationship with performance is not linearly proportional.
cards.zh:
直觉：路塞车时，大货车不会令行程快一倍。

  • 错：64-bit 比 32-bit 效率高一倍。
  • 对：64-bit 可寻址更多内存、处理更复杂功能。
  • 频率、核心数、字长都与性能非线性正比。

考试写法：A 64-bit processor can address more memory; not linearly proportional.

ex.q: Compare addressable memory: 32-bit vs 64-bit.
ex.a:
1. 32-bit: 232 B = 4 GB.
  2. 64-bit: 264 B = 16 EB (260 B = 1 EB, × 24).
  3. So the gain is mainly more addressable memory.
ex.az:
1. 32 位：4 GB。
  2. 64 位：16 EB。
  3. 主要优势是可寻址内存更大。

ex.q: A PC has 8 GB RAM and a 32-bit OS. Why can't it use all 8 GB?
ex.a:
1. 32-bit addresses reach only 232 B = 4 GB.
  2. Memory above 4 GB cannot be addressed.
ex.az:
1. 32 位只能寻址 4 GB。
  2. 超出部分用不到。

ex.q: 'Going from 4 to 8 cores halves the time of any program.' Spot the error.
ex.a:
1. Same misconception as 64-bit = 2×.
  2. Only parallel parts speed up; it is not linearly proportional.
ex.az:
1. 与“64 位=两倍”同一误解。
  2. 非线性正比。

cards.en:
Idea: RAM is a whiteboard: quick to write and wipe, but cleaned when the power goes off.

  • RAM is volatile: data disappears when the computer shuts down.
  • It stores data temporarily for processing, so its size and access rate greatly affect CPU performance.
  • Speed: slower than cache, faster than secondary storage.
  • Upgrade by adding or replacing RAM sticks; check the type (DDR3 / DDR4 / DDR5 SDRAM have different shapes and may not fit).

Exam wording: RAM is volatile and stores data temporarily for processing. Larger RAM allows more data to be processed without accessing slower secondary storage.
cards.zh:
直觉：RAM 像白板：写擦都快，但一断电就被擦干净。

  • RAM 是 volatile，关机数据消失。
  • 暂存处理中的数据，其容量和速度大大影响 CPU 表现。
  • 比 cache 慢、比 secondary storage 快。
  • 可加装/更换 RAM 条，但要配合主板（DDR3/4/5 形状不同）。

考试写法：RAM is volatile and stores data temporarily for processing.

ex.q: A PC with 4 GB RAM is slow with many browser tabs. Suggest an upgrade and explain.
ex.a:
1. Too little RAM → data is swapped to slow secondary storage.
  2. Add RAM sticks (e.g. to 16 GB) of the type the motherboard supports.
  3. More data stays in RAM, so it is faster.
ex.az:
1. RAM 不足会用到慢速储存。
  2. 加装合适规格的 RAM。
  3. 更多数据留在 RAM，较快。

ex.q: Why can't frequently updated processing data be stored in ROM?
ex.a:
1. ROM usually cannot be rewritten.
  2. Processing data changes all the time, so it needs RAM.
ex.az:
1. ROM 通常不能改写。
  2. 处理数据常变，需用 RAM。

ex.q: 'Any DDR5 stick will fit a DDR4 motherboard.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Different DDR versions have different shapes/notches.
  2. Check the motherboard design first.
ex.az:
1. 不同 DDR 形状不同。
  2. 要先看主板支持什么。

cards.tz: 只读存储器 ROM 与 BIOS
cards.en:
Idea: ROM is the printed instruction card inside a new gadget: always there, rarely changed, read when you start.

  • ROM is non-volatile; its data usually cannot be rewritten.
  • It stores firmware: instructions required to start a computer. This firmware is the BIOS (basic input/output system).
  • Printers and scanners also have ROM, but their firmware is not BIOS; it controls that device.
  • ROM is used mainly at boot, so its size barely affects performance.

Exam wording: ROM is non-volatile and stores the firmware (BIOS) required to start a computer.
cards.zh:
直觉：ROM 像新电器里印好的说明卡：一直在、很少改、开机时读。

  • ROM 是 non-volatile，通常不能改写。
  • 存放开机所需的 firmware，即 BIOS。
  • 打印机、扫描仪也有 ROM，但里面不是 BIOS。
  • ROM 只在开机时用，容量几乎不影响性能。

考试写法：ROM stores the firmware (BIOS) required to start a computer.

ex.q: What happens to the BIOS when the PC is switched off?
ex.a:
1. BIOS is in ROM.
  2. ROM is non-volatile, so the BIOS stays.
ex.az:
1. BIOS 在 ROM。
  2. 不会消失。

ex.q: Does a printer's ROM contain a BIOS?
ex.a:
1. It contains firmware.
  2. But it is the printer's own firmware, not BIOS.
ex.az:
1. 有 firmware。
  2. 不是 BIOS。

ex.q: 'Buy a PC with a bigger ROM to make games run faster.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. ROM is only used when booting.
  2. Its size barely affects performance; more RAM or a better GPU would help.
ex.az:
1. ROM 只在开机用。
  2. 应升级 RAM 或 GPU。

cards.tz: ROM 的种类及 UEFI（增润）
cards.en:
Idea: Some 'read-only' memory can be wiped with special tools, like erasing pencil vs. pen.

TypeRewrite?
PROMprogrammed once, cannot be rewritten
EPROMerased by ultraviolet light
EEPROMerased by electricity

UEFI (unified extensible firmware interface) is a newer alternative to BIOS and may perform better.

Exam wording: EPROM can be erased by ultraviolet light; EEPROM can be erased electrically. UEFI is an alternative firmware to BIOS.
cards.zh:
直觉：有些“只读”内存可用特殊方法擦掉，像铅笔字可擦。

种类可否改写
PROM写一次，不能改
EPROM用紫外光擦除
EEPROM用电擦除

UEFI 是较新的 BIOS 替代品。

考试写法：EEPROM can be erased electrically.

ex.q: A BIOS update is installed by software. Which ROM type allows this?
ex.a:
1. Software can only use electricity, not UV light.
  2. So EEPROM (flash).
ex.az:
1. 软件只能用电擦写。
  2. EEPROM。

ex.q: Match: needs UV lamp / write once / erase electrically.
ex.a:
1. UV → EPROM.
  2. Once → PROM.
  3. Electric → EEPROM.
ex.az:
1. EPROM
  2. PROM
  3. EEPROM

ex.q: 'All ROM can never be changed.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. ROM usually isn't rewritten in normal use.
  2. But EPROM and EEPROM can be erased with special methods.
ex.az:
1. 一般不改写。
  2. EPROM、EEPROM 可擦除。

cards.tz: 存取方法：顺序存取与直接存取
cards.en:
Idea: A cassette tape: to hear song 5, you wind past songs 1–4 (sequential). A playlist: tap song 5 directly (direct).

Sequential accessDirect (random) access
Howsearch from the start, in ordereach position has a unique address; go straight there
Speedvaries with position; lower on averagehigher and stable
Devicesmagnetic tapehard disk, SSD, USB flash drive, optical disk

Exam wording: In sequential access, data is searched sequentially from the beginning, so the access rate varies with location. In direct access, each position has a unique address, so data is accessed directly.
cards.zh:
直觉：卡带要听第 5 首，必须先卷过 1–4 首（顺序）；播放列表可直接点第 5 首（直接）。

SequentialDirect
方法由头按次序搜寻每个位置有唯一地址，直接到达
速度随位置变化，平均较慢较快稳定
设备磁带硬盘、SSD、U 盘、光盘

考试写法：Direct access: each position has a unique address, so data is accessed directly.

ex.q: Records are on tape; reading one takes 2 s. How long to reach record 5 (sequential)?
ex.a:
1. Must pass records 1–4 first, then read 5.
  2. 5 × 2 = 10 s. Record 1 takes only 2 s, so time varies.
ex.az:
1. 要先经过 1–4。
  2. 5×2=10 秒，随位置变化。

ex.q: Why is magnetic tape fine for backups?
ex.a:
1. Backups are written and read in order, rarely searched.
  2. Tape's large size and low unit price matter more than speed.
ex.az:
1. 备份按顺序读写。
  2. 容量大、便宜更重要。

ex.q: 'Hard disks use sequential access because the disk spins.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Spinning does not mean sequential.
  2. Heads move straight to the unique address: direct access.
ex.az:
1. 旋转不等于顺序。
  2. 磁头直接到地址，是 direct access。

cards.t: Magnetic storage: magnetic tape and hard disk
cards.en:
Idea: Both store data as tiny magnets. Tape is a long ribbon (cheap, slow to reach). A hard disk is a spinning plate with a moving arm (faster).

  • Magnetic tape: plastic film with magnetic coating; size in TB; low unit price; sequential only, slow due to tape winding → used for backup; damaged by humidity.
  • Hard disk: metal platters + read/write heads; direct access, faster than tape; heads do not touch the disk, but it is prone to damage on impact (moving parts).

Exam wording: Magnetic tape has a low data access rate due to tape winding, so it is used for backup. A hard disk uses read/write heads to move directly to data.
cards.zh:
直觉：两者都用微小磁性记录。磁带是长带（便宜、找得慢）；硬盘是旋转盘片加移动臂（较快）。

  • 磁带：容量以 TB 计、单价低、只能顺序存取、卷带耗时 → 用于备份；怕潮湿。
  • 硬盘：金属盘片 + read/write heads，direct access；有活动部件，怕撞击。

考试写法：Tape: low access rate due to tape winding, used for backup.

ex.q: A tape holds 18 TB; 1 TB = 2<sup>40</sup> bytes. How many bytes?
A bank backs up 500 TB nightly. Tape or SSD?
ex.a:
1. Huge size, read rarely, cost matters.
  2. Tape: large and low unit price; speed not critical.
ex.az:
1. 容量大、少读取、重成本。
  2. 选磁带。

ex.q: 'A laptop hard disk is safe to drop because the heads never touch the disk.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. A shock can make the heads hit the platters.
  2. Hard disks are prone to damage on impact.
ex.az:
1. 撞击会令磁头碰到盘片。
  2. 硬盘怕撞击。

cards.t: Solid-state storage: SSD, memory card, USB flash drive
cards.tz: 固态储存：SSD、记忆卡、U 盘
cards.en:
Idea: No spinning, no moving arm: just chips. Like switching from a record player to a phone's music.

  • SSD = flash memory + controller. Flash memory is read and written electrically at high speed.
  • No moving parts → more durable, portable, less energy; but higher unit price per capacity.
  • Memory card: small flash memory for cameras/phones; SD/microSD format.
  • USB flash drive: flash memory + USB interface; for backup and data transfer.

Exam wording: An SSD has no moving parts, so it is more durable and consumes less energy than a hard disk, but it has a higher unit price per capacity.
cards.zh:
直觉：没有转盘、没有活动臂，只有芯片。

  • SSD = flash memory + controller，用电快速读写。
  • 没有活动部件 → 耐用、便携、省电；但每单位容量较贵。
  • Memory card：相机/手机用，SD/microSD。
  • U 盘：flash + USB 接口，用于备份和传送资料。

考试写法：An SSD has no moving parts, so it is more durable.

ex.q: A 1 TB SSD costs $600, a 4 TB hard disk $800. Unit price per TB?
ex.a:
1. SSD: 600 ÷ 1 = $600/TB.
  2. HDD: 800 ÷ 4 = $200/TB.
  3. SSD costs 3× per TB.
ex.az:
1. SSD 600/TB。
  2. HDD 200/TB。
  3. SSD 每 TB 贵 3 倍。

ex.q: Give two reasons a field reporter prefers an SSD laptop.
ex.a:
1. Durable: no moving parts, survives knocks.
  2. Less energy: longer battery life (and faster access).
ex.az:
1. 耐用。
  2. 省电。

ex.q: 'An SSD is magnetic storage like a hard disk.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong medium.
  2. SSD uses flash memory (solid-state).
ex.az:
1. 介质错。
  2. SSD 用 flash memory。

cards.en:
Idea: Data is tiny bumps and grooves on a shiny disc; a laser reads them like a finger reading braille.

  • Plastic disc with a reflective coating; data as grooves, read by a laser beam.
  • Scratches can divert the laser and corrupt data.
DiscSize
CD~700 MB
DVD~4.7 GB
Blu-ray (BD)25–128 GB
Read onlyWrite onceRewritable
-ROM-R-RW / BD-RE

Exam wording: Data is represented by grooves and read by laser beams; scratches may divert the laser and corrupt data.
cards.zh:
直觉：数据是光盘上的微小凹槽，激光像手指摸盲文一样读出。

  • 塑胶盘 + 反光层，数据为凹槽，以激光读取。
  • 刮花会令激光偏离、数据损坏。
  • CD≈700 MB；DVD≈4.7 GB；BD 25–128 GB。
  • -ROM 只读；-R 写一次；-RW/BD-RE 可重写。

考试写法：Scratches may divert the laser beam and corrupt data.

ex.q: How many CDs (700 MB) are needed for a 4.7 GB file? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
A publisher sells software that buyers must not change. Which disc type?
ex.a:
1. Content fixed at the factory.
  2. -ROM (e.g. DVD-ROM).
ex.az:
1. 内容固定。
  2. 用 ROM 类。

ex.q: 'CD-R can be erased and rewritten many times.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. R = recordable once.
  2. Rewritable is CD-RW.
ex.az:
1. R 只能写一次。
  2. 可重写是 CD-RW。

cards.en:
Idea: No device wins everything. Match the device to the need: cheap and huge, fast and tough, or easy to hand out.

TapeHard diskSSDOptical
Mediummagneticmagneticflashoptical
Sizevery largelargemediumsmall
Unit pricelowlowhighlow–medium
Accesssequentialdirectdirectdirect
Access rateunstable, lowestmediumhighmedium
Weaknesshumidityimpactpricescratches

Exam wording: Always link the property to the scenario, e.g. SSD: higher data access rate and more durable as it has no moving parts.
cards.zh:
直觉：没有一种设备样样最好，要按需要配对。

磁带硬盘SSD光盘
容量极大大中小
单价低低高低–中
存取顺序直接直接直接
速度最慢、不稳中高中
弱点潮湿撞击价钱刮花

考试写法：答案要连系情境，如 SSD has a higher data access rate and is more durable。

ex.q: Choose a device: (i) archive 200 TB of CCTV; (ii) OS drive for a fast laptop; (iii) give a brochure video to 500 visitors.
ex.a:
1. Tape: very large, low unit price.
  2. SSD: high access rate, durable.
  3. Optical disc: low cost per copy, easy to hand out.
ex.az:
1. 磁带。
  2. SSD。
  3. 光盘。

ex.q: Rank by access rate, fastest first: hard disk, tape, SSD.
ex.a: 1. SSD > hard disk > tape.
ex.az: 1. SSD > 硬盘 > 磁带。

ex.q: 'Use an SSD for backups because it is fastest.' Why is this weak?
ex.a:
1. Speed is not the main need for backup.
  2. Large size and low unit price matter more → tape/hard disk.
ex.az:
1. 备份不重速度。
  2. 容量大、便宜更重要。

cards.en:
Idea: Two people copying the same notes: if one loses theirs, the other still has it. Or two people each writing half the notes: done twice as fast.

  • RAID (redundant array of independent disks) combines multiple storage devices (hard disks, SSDs).
  • Purposes: higher data transfer rate; error detection; less chance of data loss when a device fails.
  • Not a must in a system unit; common in servers and NAS.

Exam wording: RAID combines multiple storage devices to improve the data transfer rate and reduce the chance of data loss due to device failure.
cards.zh:
直觉：两个人抄同一份笔记，一人遗失另一人仍有；或者各抄一半，快一倍。

  • RAID 把多个储存设备组合起来。
  • 目的：提高传输率、错误检测、减少设备故障导致的数据损失。
  • 不是必须，常见于 server 和 NAS。

考试写法：RAID improves the data transfer rate and reduces the chance of data loss due to device failure.

ex.q: A 1 GB file; one disk writes at 200 MB/s. Split across 2 disks writing at the same time (striping). Time? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
ex.a:
1. One disk: 1024 ÷ 200 = 5.12 s.
  2. Two disks each write 512 MB: 512 ÷ 200 = 2.56 s.
  3. Transfer rate is doubled (ideal).
ex.az:
1. 单碟 5.12 秒。
  2. 两碟各 512 MB：2.56 秒。

ex.q: Two disks hold the same copy (mirroring). Disk 1 fails. What happens?
ex.a:
1. Disk 2 still has every file.
  2. No data is lost; replace disk 1 and copy back.
ex.az:
1. Disk 2 仍有全部资料。
  2. 不会丢失。

ex.q: 'With RAID you never need a backup.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. RAID protects against disk failure only.
  2. Deleting a file or a virus affects all disks; still keep a separate backup.
ex.az:
1. RAID 只防硬件故障。
  2. 误删、病毒仍需备份。

frames.en: The controller writes the same data to both disks.
frames.zh: 控制器把相同数据写到两块碟。

frames.en: Disk 1 fails; disk 2 still has the data.
frames.zh: Disk 1 故障，Disk 2 仍有数据。

frames.en: Data is split: half to each disk at the same time, so it is faster.
frames.zh: 数据分成两半同时写入，较快。

cards.t: Network storage: NAS and cloud storage
cards.tz: 网络储存：NAS 与云端储存
cards.en:
Idea: NAS is a shared bookshelf in your office. Cloud storage is a rented locker you can open from anywhere with Internet.

NASCloud storage
Whatfile server with many drives in a RAIDservice from a provider (e.g. ISP)
Accessusers on the LAN, many at the same timeanytime, anywhere with Internet
Costbuy onceregular fee, more for more space

Exam wording: NAS allows users on a LAN to read and write at the same time. Cloud storage allows users to access data anytime and anywhere with an Internet connection, but may need regular payment.
cards.zh:
直觉：NAS 是办公室里共享的书架；云端储存是租来的储物柜，只要有网络随处可开。

NASCloud
是什么多碟组成 RAID 的 file server服务商提供的服务
存取LAN 内多人同时有网络即可随时随地
成本一次性定期付费

考试写法：NAS: users on a LAN read and write at the same time. Cloud: anytime and anywhere with Internet, regular payment.

ex.q: Cloud costs $50/month; a NAS costs $1500. After how many months is the NAS cheaper?
ex.a:
1. 1500 ÷ 50 = 30.
  2. After 30 months the NAS costs less (ignoring power/repairs).
ex.az:
1. 1500÷50=30。
  2. 30 个月后 NAS 较便宜。

ex.q: Staff work from home often. NAS or cloud?
ex.a:
1. Need access outside the office.
  2. Cloud: anywhere with Internet.
ex.az:
1. 需在外存取。
  2. 云端。

ex.q: 'NAS lets anyone on the Internet open the files by default.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. NAS works on the LAN.
  2. Outside access needs extra setup.
ex.az:
1. NAS 在 LAN 内用。
  2. 外部存取要另外设定。

cards.en:
Idea: A pyramid. The top is tiny, fast and expensive (your pocket). The bottom is huge, slow and cheap (a warehouse).

  1. Register
  2. Cache memory
  3. RAM
  4. SSD
  5. Hard disk
  6. Magnetic tape

Higher = higher access rate, smaller size, higher unit price per capacity. Lower = the opposite.

Exam wording: The higher the storage is located in the hierarchy, the higher its data access rate, the smaller its storage size and the higher its unit price per capacity.
cards.zh:
直觉：金字塔：顶部小、快、贵（口袋）；底部大、慢、便宜（货仓）。

  1. Register
  2. Cache
  3. RAM
  4. SSD
  5. Hard disk
  6. Magnetic tape

越高：越快、越小、单价越高；越低相反。

考试写法：The higher the storage is located, the higher its data access rate, the smaller its storage size and the higher its unit price per capacity.

ex.q: Order from smallest to largest typical size: RAM, register, hard disk, cache.
ex.a:
1. Follow the hierarchy top to bottom.
  2. Register < cache < RAM < hard disk.
ex.az:
1. 由上而下。
  2. Register < cache < RAM < hard disk。

ex.q: Which has the higher unit price per GB: RAM or hard disk? Why?
ex.a:
1. RAM is higher in the hierarchy.
  2. So RAM costs more per GB.
ex.az:
1. RAM 层级较高。
  2. 每 GB 较贵。

ex.q: 'Cache is bigger than RAM because it is faster.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Faster means smaller and pricier, not bigger.
  2. Cache is smaller than RAM.
ex.az:
1. 越快越小。
  2. Cache 比 RAM 小。

frames.en: Register: fastest, tiny, inside the CPU.
frames.zh: Register：最快、最小，在 CPU 内。

frames.en: Cache: very fast, small, in the CPU.
frames.zh: Cache：很快、小。

frames.en: RAM: main memory for running programs.
frames.zh: RAM：运行程序的主存。

frames.en: SSD: fast secondary storage.
frames.zh: SSD：快速辅助储存。

frames.en: Hard disk: large and cheap.
frames.zh: Hard disk：大而便宜。

frames.en: Magnetic tape: largest, cheapest, slowest; for backup.
frames.zh: Magnetic tape：最大、最便宜、最慢，用于备份。

cards.en:
Idea: Bigger body = room for more power and storage; smaller body = easier to carry.

DesktopLaptopTablet
Screennone built in; can be largemediumsmall
Portabilitylowmediumhigh
Computing powerhighmediumlow
Storagelargemediumsmall
Built-in devicesnonemonitor, keyboard, touchpad, speakers, mic, webcamtouchscreen, speakers, mic, camera

Smartphones, smart TVs, game consoles, smartwatches and smartglasses are computers too. Tablets usually use less energy.

Exam wording: A desktop has higher computing power and larger storage but low portability; a tablet has high portability but lower computing power.
cards.zh:
直觉：机身越大，越能放强劲的零件；越小越方便携带。

台式机笔记本平板
便携低中高
运算高中低
储存大中小
内置设备无屏幕、键盘、触控板等触控屏、镜头等

手机、智能电视、游戏机、智能手表也是电脑。平板较省电。

考试写法：A desktop has higher computing power but low portability; a tablet has high portability.

ex.q: A film editor works only in the studio. Desktop, laptop or tablet?
ex.a:
1. Needs high computing power and storage.
  2. Does not need to move.
  3. Desktop.
ex.az:
1. 需高运算和大储存。
  2. 不需移动。
  3. 台式机。

ex.q: A delivery worker needs to scan and sign on the road. Which?
ex.a:
1. Portability and a touchscreen matter most.
  2. Tablet.
ex.az:
1. 便携和触控最重要。
  2. 平板。

ex.q: 'A smart TV is not a computer because it has no keyboard.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. It has a processor, memory and runs apps.
  2. It can use a virtual keyboard; it can function as a computer.
ex.az:
1. 它有处理器、内存，能运行程序。
  2. 可用虚拟键盘，算是电脑。

cards.en:
Idea: Start from the job, then pick the specs that help that job. Don't pay for what you won't use.

  1. Find the main task (word processing, video editing, travel…).
  2. Performance factors: CPU clock rate, number of cores, RAM size, GPU (dedicated vs integrated), SSD vs HDD.
  3. Non-performance factors: weight, screen size, price.
  4. Give 2 points linked to the scenario.

Number of ports and ROM size do not affect performance much.

Exam wording: e.g. Model B is more suitable because it has a dedicated graphics card, which provides higher graphics processing power for video editing.
cards.zh:
直觉：先看用途，再选对用途有帮助的规格，不要为用不上的东西付钱。

  1. 找出主要用途。
  2. 性能因素：clock rate、核心数、RAM、GPU、SSD/HDD。
  3. 非性能因素：重量、屏幕、价钱。
  4. 写 2 点并连系情境。

端口数量、ROM 大小对性能影响不大。

考试写法：如 Model B has a dedicated graphics card, which provides higher graphics processing power for video editing.

ex.q: Model A: 2.4 GHz 4-core, 8 GB, HDD, iGPU, 1.2 kg. Model B: 3.6 GHz 8-core, 32 GB, SSD, graphics card, 2.5 kg. For video editing?
ex.a:
1. Video editing needs CPU power, RAM and GPU.
  2. B has more cores/higher clock rate and a dedicated graphics card.
  3. Choose B; weight is less important in a studio.
ex.az:
1. 剪片需 CPU、RAM、GPU。
  2. B 核心多、有独立显卡。
  3. 选 B。

ex.q: Same models, for a student who types notes and travels daily?
ex.a:
1. Light tasks; carried daily.
  2. A: lighter (1.2 kg) and cheaper; iGPU is enough for word processing.
ex.az:

cards.tz: 计算机系统：硬件与软件
cards.en:
Intuition: Think of a piano and sheet music. The piano (hardware) makes the sound, but without music (software) it just sits there.

  • Hardware = the physical parts you can touch: CPU, RAM, monitor, keyboard.
  • Software = data or instructions that tell the hardware what to do.
  • Both are needed: hardware without software does nothing; software needs hardware to run on.

Software has two types: system software (looks after the machine) and application software (does a job for the user).

Exam wording: A computer system consists of hardware and software. Hardware is the physical parts of the computer. Software is the data or instructions designed to help the computer accomplish specific tasks.
cards.zh:
直觉理解：钢琴和乐谱：钢琴（hardware）发声，但没有乐谱（software）就弹不出曲子。

  • Hardware（硬件）：摸得到的物理部件，如 CPU、RAM、显示器、键盘。
  • Software（软件）：告诉硬件做什么的数据或指令。
  • 两者缺一不可。

软件分两类：system software（照顾机器本身）和 application software（帮用户完成具体工作）。

Exam wording（考试写法）：A computer system consists of hardware and software. Software is the data or instructions designed to help the computer accomplish specific tasks.
